claims.statement: Termind separates Swift Testing by ownership: FrameworkTests protects portable shared-framework contracts, TFMTests covers macOS composition/native interaction/remote-session behavior, and TFITests covers mobile composition, scene behavior, and mobile presentation.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests protects import and model ownership, rejects local AgentKit type redefinitions, and checks that all three CloudKit coordinators retain the shared safety gates while the lifecycle stays independent of SwiftData and Persistence imports.

MobileWorkspaceStore persists a versioned device-local descriptor snapshot containing only IDs, host references, titles and kinds; migration preserves legacy values while discarding duplicate indices. Invalid, unknown-version or duplicate-ID data prevents saves until a successful load and preserves original bytes.
Mobile workspace restoration does not persist credentials, commands, or live session state.

Mobile app tests establish that conversations are shared across scenes while assistant navigation, selection, and drafts are scene-local, and that external connection workspaces are ephemeral rather than Vault or saved-workspace records.

SFTPTransferContext lets queued transfers retain an authenticated primary connection after the UI owner releases it, closes that connection only when no owner or transfers remain, and opens additional connections from a snapshot through a noninteractive request.

Transfer-context tests verify bounded per-host scheduling across multiple contexts, silent connection fallback behavior, and that cancellation or a retired generation does not trigger the PTY fallback.

Security regression fixtures verify that agent authentication can use one-use credentials without mutating Vault state unless saving is requested, collect jump-host and destination authentication in route order, and coalesce concurrent authentication while preventing SFTP opening after cancellation.

SSH interaction-policy tests require forbidden requests to fail rather than show host-key or keyboard-interactive UI; additional connection snapshots retain references instead of credential material, and clearing a connection configuration consumes secret values shared by copies.

Persistence compatibility tests open historical SwiftData fixtures through the shared container factory, assert retained records and migration outcomes through V34, and verify independent in-memory containers expose the full schema. The direct V31-to-V34 fixture also verifies preserved Identity configuration/journal dates, event-origin backfill and default workspace preferences; V32 and V33 are not distributed endpoints.

Agent replay persistence tests verify frozen context/tool-result restoration, prevent replay-row duplication across later snapshots, remove replay backing on conversation deletion, and preserve a durable result recorded before the next snapshot.
MacOS tests that show windows or take focus must use the requiresVisibleWindow trait, which is enabled only by TERMIND_WINDOW_TESTS=1; normal test runs therefore skip them.

CloudKit safety fixtures use fake transport with real category coordinators, journals, record coding, batches and providers to verify incompatible-record blocking, compatible progress, conflict parity, retry/restart, tombstones/recreation, rollback and status-reason distinctions.

Disk-backed safety tests cover V30-to-V31 migration, legacy quarantine import and reopening interrupted pending state; lifecycle tests cover persistence/lookup failures, retired engines, overlapping callbacks and recovery gating, without claiming live CloudKit delivery.

Focused connection-history tests cover V31-to-V34 migration, the independent generic device record and rename propagation, synchronized event lifecycle/tombstones, stable local-device filtering, newest-250 storage, 100-event desktop and 50-event mobile presentation, preferred-protocol quick actions and multilingual mobile rendering while excluding Serial.

The same-run SwiftData edit regression uses equal timestamps, reversed UUIDs, compacted production restoration, legacy and unknown tool ownership, backing-row counts, staging adoption and late-write attempts; the empty-run regression separately proves live/restored ordering when the replacement clock moves backward.

Failed/interrupted staging-adoption tests verify one real message/run/replay graph and restore provenance, state, failure and frozen context from a new ModelContext and repository over the same in-memory container rather than proving disk relaunch.

Composer regression covers compacted same-run display-prefix, tool, title, plan, compaction and run chronology retention; mobile exercises SwiftData restore and operations edit to compare live and restored prefix ownership.

Conversation operations reject a non-user replacement without invoking truncation and preserve visible messages and transcript when an injected repository truncation rejects; controller edit-failure and post-edit cancellation tests check captured replacement context, preserved history, and interrupted real-run adoption of staging. These port-level failures do not inject real SwiftData transaction faults.

Captured missing-model or missing-credential preparation failures construct a failed snapshot and keep preparation active until an asynchronous repository save succeeds; only then does the live conversation record failure, while a save error appends an assistant error instead. Controller tests gate the save and verify joining/projection ordering; missing-credential and navigation tests separately wait for a recorded failed save attempt, which does not itself prove save completion.

Manual compaction is refused while agent preparation is held at a memory snapshot barrier, without starting compaction activity; edit and cancellation fixtures also prohibit stale or cancelled prepared edits from entering truncation and join in-flight truncation before recording interruption.

After an edited replacement commits, a pending failed-run save blocks further edit and fork and later adopts the real failed-run ownership; if that save instead throws, preparation retires without adopting staging or recording a completed failed snapshot and displays an assistant error.

Tool presentation regression tests protect the composed AgentKit/Termind presenter ID namespace, equivalent restored and legacy card detail, safe decoding of older metadata, and structured approval details that include provided command/input rather than promising redaction.

MCP upload tests exercise scoped ticket capacity, acknowledged-offset resume and full digest, stream backpressure, cancellation and cleanup, conflict and terminal status with a fake SFTP client and controllable clock; a loopback HTTP test sends fresh and resumed bodies beyond the ordinary MCP body limit without a real remote SFTP server.

MobileBackgroundController retires a background lease once; platform-spy tests cover repeated/stale expiration, synchronous reentrant expiration during begin that preserves a replacement lease, and invalid task identifiers that expire without ending a UIKit task.

MobileCardTests verifies card width/accessibility column policy and stable measured heights offscreen, while exercising saved-host timestamp and draft-color persistence through an in-memory MobileAppModel rather than requiring a UIKit key window.

Mobile key-window integration suites are opt-in and must run without parallel testing because UIKit presentation state is process-wide; StoreKit tests require separate manual opt-in, and macOS visible-window tests retain their own opt-in gate.
